report.source_text: MR image was obtained and showed a small spherical lesion at right subcortical occipital lobe showing different intensities (Fig. 2). Lesion was hypointense on T1-weighted image, hyperintense rim on T2-weighted image. Ring enhancement was noted on the contrast enhanced T1 and blooming artefact on SWI. These findings suggesting granular nodular stage. Other multiple singular lesions were seen at left juxtacortical temporal lobe, right juxtacortical parietal lobe and left thalamus showing different intensities (Figs. 3, and 4). Lesion was also hypointense on T1-weighted image with no signal on T2-weighted image, with blooming artefact on SWI which suggesting nodular calcified stage. No restricted area was seen within the lesion on DWI-ADC on both stages.

report.source_text: MR Spectroscopy was conducted (Fig. 5). Minor shift scale (approximately -0.5 ppm) was made based on major resonances of N-acetylaspartate (NAA), creatine (Cr), and choline (Cho) in the spectroscopy control from the normal parenchyma. Increase in lactate and decrease in choline and N-acetylaspartate were seen which suggesting diagnosis of an inflammatory lesion. Levels of NAA/Cr ratio (0.38) and Cho/Cr ratio (1.21) were seen to be below 1.5.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 71-year-old man presented with 4 months of intermittent headaches and abrupt vision loss, along with chronic left extremity weakness following a stroke 1 year prior. Initial workup revealed normal routine laboratories and negative HIV serology. Brain CT demonstrated multiple calcified nodules (nodular calcified stage) in the right subcortical parietal lobe, left thalamus, and left basal ganglia, plus a granular nodular stage lesion in the right cortical-subcortical occipital lobe. Brain MRI confirmed these findings, showing a right subcortical occipital spherical lesion with T1 hypointensity, T2 hyperintense rim, ring enhancement on contrast, and blooming on SWI consistent with granular nodular stage, along with additional lesions in the left juxtacortical temporal lobe, right juxtacortical parietal lobe, and left thalamus showing T1 hypointensity with T2 signal loss and SWI blooming consistent with nodular calcified stage. No restricted diffusion was observed on DWI-ADC sequences. MR spectroscopy demonstrated increased lactate with decreased choline and N-acetylaspartate (NAA/Cr ratio 0.38, Cho/Cr ratio 1.21), consistent with an inflammatory lesion. The constellation of multiple parenchymal lesions in different evolutionary stages (calcified and granular nodular) with characteristic imaging features established the diagnosis of neurocysticercosis.
